issue.title: [M5][SM-505] Final WebGPU default-backend promotion and release acceptance
issue.body:
## Objective
Make the evidence-based final decision to promote WebGPU as Steel Moth's default `Auto` renderer and package the first release that satisfies functional, visual, performance, fallback, and deployment gates.

## Scope
Reconcile SM-405 functional parity with SM-500/501 target-hardware performance evidence; verify packaging/static/PWA cache identity; clean-extraction checks; review unresolved renderer blockers; update backend default only if gates pass; produce final validation/performance/memory/release reports.

## Non-goals
- No new fidelity feature work.
- No opportunistic algorithm rewrite unless required to close a release-blocking defect.
- Do not weaken performance/visual gates silently to obtain a release.

## Dependencies / concurrency
Depends on SM-405 functional parity, SM-500 instrumentation, SM-501 target-hardware quality/performance acceptance, and all implementation issues required by the intended first WebGPU release. This is the final promotion gate; later GTAO/SSGI/volumetric milestones do not block the initial WebGPU-primary release unless explicitly pulled into its scope.

## Canonical context
Read `docs/WEBGPU_VALIDATION_PLAN.md` release gates, `docs/MASTER_WEBGPU_PROGRAMME.md`, `docs/DEPENDENCY_AND_CONCURRENCY.md`, and `AGENTS.md`.

## Implementation prompt
Assemble existing evidence rather than generating optimistic summaries. Confirm Gates A–F, WebGL2 fallback, deterministic fixtures, editor/room invalidation, Chrome/Firefox correctness, GTX 1650 Super timing, version/cache/deployment identity, and clean-package extraction. If all required evidence passes, change `Auto` to prefer WebGPU and produce a release candidate; otherwise leave the default unchanged and record the blockers.

## Acceptance criteria
- SM-405 functional parity is complete.
- Target-hardware benchmark satisfies the documented timing targets or a separately reviewed architecture decision has revised them with evidence.
- No open release-blocking WebGPU validation/ownership/editor/fallback defect remains.
- WebGL2 compatibility fallback remains runnable.
- Static/PWA deployment cannot silently serve stale renderer/material assets.
- Clean extracted package reruns required tests successfully.
- `Auto` is promoted to WebGPU only when all required gates pass.

## Verification
Fresh Chrome/Firefox profiles where practical; full deterministic fixture/cross-browser matrix; three-run target benchmark dataset; inherited and WebGPU suites; clean-build/package/extract/retest; version/cache audit.

## Expected artifacts
`docs/WEBGPU_RELEASE_VALIDATION.md`, `docs/PERFORMANCE_REPORT_WEBGPU_PRIMARY.md`, renderer-memory report, final captures, changelog/migration notes, release/package artifacts and checksums as repository workflow supports.

## Blocking / stopping conditions
Any unresolved Gate A–F failure, missing target-hardware evidence, stale-asset/deployment defect, fallback failure, or ambiguous package validation keeps `Auto` unchanged and this issue open.
